form.dataset.none: Create or choose a dataset on the Datasets page first.

form.paRun.none: No succeeded PA run on this dataset yet.

run.next.succeeded: Open the result to see metrics with their evidence type.
run.next.queued: Waiting for a free device. Cancel if you no longer need it.
run.artifacts.empty: Artifacts are registered when the run finishes.
run.artifacts.incomplete: One or more required artifacts are missing; the manifest is incomplete.
logs.none.stored: No log is stored for this run. Runs imported from a share package have no worker log; the package says so under redaction.
results.title: Results
results.empty: No results yet. A result is written when a PA or DPD run succeeds.
settings.title: Settings
settings.devices.note: Detected means the driver reports the device. Tested means a model has recorded evidence on it. One does not imply the other.
settings.language.note: Applies immediately and is remembered in this workspace. Interface text and generated explanations follow this language; original technical records retain their source text.
gallery.title: Component gallery
gallery.body: Every domain component rendered on fixed mock fixtures generated from the contract examples. Nothing here is a computed result.
gallery.perf: Performance probe: PSD with {psd} points × {traces} traces and an I/Q window of {iq} samples rendered in {ms} ms.
diff.title: Configuration differences
chart.spectrum.title: Power spectral density
chart.iq.title: I/Q time window
datasets.import.title: Import my data
datasets.import.upload.help: CSV only: UTF-8, at most 25 MiB and 1,000,000 paired samples.
datasets.import.noFiles: No CSV / .npy / .npz files here. Copy files into the import root or upload one.
datasets.import.mapping.help: Which column holds each logical signal. Guessed from the headers; fix any mistake here, including swapped I/Q.
datasets.import.signal.help: Needed by the evaluation profile; without them formal metrics are blocked, not guessed.
datasets.import.name: Display name
datasets.detail.versions.empty: Only raw-v1 (built-in datasets keep their original split).
datasets.detail.doctor.empty: No report yet. The doctor checks NaN/Inf, length, outliers, clipping plateaus, delay, gain, amplitude, bandwidth and metadata, and says which evaluations would be unreliable.
datasets.detail.doctor.blocked: Formal evaluation is blocked until the error items are resolved.
datasets.preprocess.title: Preprocess (creates a new version)
datasets.preprocess.help: Raw files are never modified. Preview first; a version is written only when you confirm. Normalisation is fitted on the training split only.
datasets.preprocess.normalize: Normalise by the training-split input peak
datasets.import.pick: Pick a file on the left (or upload one) to inspect it.
datasets.preprocess.version.help: Letters, digits, dots, dashes; e.g. aligned-v1. Cannot overwrite an existing version.
results.detail.profile.help: Same output, different score definitions. Select the same calculation for fair comparisons.
results.detail.definitions.help: What each score means under {profile} v{version}. Names, formulas and better-directions come from the registry, not from the page.
form.profile.help: Training evaluates and selects checkpoints using valid-sample metrics. The legacy protocol reproduces historical results; padded tails can inflate leakage.
form.import.help: A JSON experiment configuration (exported from a run or written by hand). It is validated by the server and submitted as is.
form.imported: Imported configuration from {source}. The server validates and runs the configuration shown below. You can change the optional name; discard the import to use the recipe form.
run.lineage.help: Read from resolved configurations: which checkpoints this run used and which runs used it.
run.lineage.empty: This run neither uses nor is used by another run.
run.apply: Apply DPD to the test split…
run.apply.title: Apply this DPD to the test split
run.apply.help: Apply the trained DPD to test input x, export its output u, and inspect the PA model’s predicted output y = PA(u). A physical PA measurement is a separate step.
run.apply.surrogate.training: PA model used for DPD training ({run})
run.apply.surrogate.help: Another succeeded PA run of the same dataset gives a new, separately stored result; the DPD's own result is never overwritten.
run.measure.title: Score captures of a physical PA driven by this export
run.measure.help: You played this run's exported u = DPD(x) (and, under the same conditions, x itself) through a PA and captured the output with an I/Q analyser. Upload the capture files and declare the set-up. OpenDPD aligns each capture to what was played (integer delay, one complex gain), scores it as captured under every profile and stores the captures with their hashes.
run.measure.attestation: The result will be labelled as a user-provided measurement, not independently verified by OpenDPD. Keep the output power, waveform and operating point identical between the two captures; any level difference is reported, never normalised away.
run.measure.with.help: PA output while u = DPD(x) was played. UTF-8 CSV with re,im or I_out,Q_out columns, up to 25 MiB. Required.
run.measure.without.help: PA output while x was played directly, same conditions. Optional; it becomes the measured baseline.
run.measure.drive.help: Generator level and PA input drive as set
run.measure.chain.help: Generator → PA → attenuation → analyser, as wired, with instrument identities
run.measure.rate.help: Rate of the capture files; the dataset rate is prefilled
run.measure.playback.help: Looped playback lets the aligned window wrap around the file
results.detail.chain.help: x is the target input, u = DPD(x) the pre-distorted PA input, y the PA output. A simulated stage comes from a learned surrogate, never from a measurement.
results.detail.baselines.help: Every column is scored against the same linear target reference_gain · x, with the same profile and valid range. Nothing is normalised separately, so power differences stay visible.
results.detail.measurement.level: Output level with DPD relative to without: {db} dB (capture units).
results.detail.measurement.level.warn: The captures are not at the same output level, so their difference is not attributable to the DPD alone.
results.detail.coverage.body: Largest fitted |x| {fitted} · peak |u| {peak} · {fraction} of the pre-distorted samples above the fitted peak.
results.detail.scaling.body: Amplitude units: {units} · input scaling: {scaling} · reference gain: {gain}.
results.detail.scaling.uncalibrated: No physical calibration: absolute output power (dBm) and efficiency are not derived from these numbers.
run.metrics.fitted: This run finished without per-epoch metrics: the model was fitted in one step (a least-squares baseline). Open the result for its scores and the fit record.
run.metrics.apply: This run scored stored weights (a DPD applied to the test split, a PA model on another condition, or measured captures); there is no training history. Open the result for the signal chain and the scores.
results.charts.help: Drawn from plots-v1 data the worker computed from the evaluated arrays (the spectral profile's Welch estimator). Hiding a trace in the legend changes nothing in the evaluation.
results.charts.none: No derived plot data for this result (it was evaluated before plots-v1). Re-evaluate the run to produce it.
chart.am.title: AM-AM
chart.pm.title: AM-PM
compare.title: Compare results
compare.pick: Pick at least two results on the Results page to compare them.
compare.comparable: Same protocol: these results may be ranked; the best value per metric is marked.
compare.incompatible: Different protocols: the results are shown side by side and are not ranked.
compare.spectrum.mismatch: The results were evaluated on different frequency axes; no overlay is drawn.
run.metrics.fromHistory: Curves come from the run's history log.
results.export.help: A package carries the resolved configuration, the results under every profile, the plot data, the checkpoints of every referenced run, the reports and the commands to reproduce. Full is private and complete; share leaves your PA data, worker logs and machine paths out and says so.
experiments.import.help: An experiment package exported by OpenDPD Studio (.zip). Every file hash is verified before anything is written; a damaged or unsupported package is refused with the reason.
logs.capped: Only the last {max} lines are kept in the viewer; older lines are in the downloadable log.
robustness.title: Robustness across conditions
robustness.intro: Adaptation reports under the conditions-v1 protocol: one device, one varied dimension, every cell of the matrix kept (failures included). Reports are built from the command line and read here; nothing is recomputed.
robustness.empty: No adaptation report in this workspace yet. Register a plan and build one with `opendpd adaptation plan … && opendpd adaptation run … && opendpd adaptation report …`.
robustness.list.label: Adaptation reports
robustness.bar.detail: {n} conditions (bar {min}); independent capture batches: {independent}; measured origin: {measured}
robustness.bar.rehearsal: Below the evidence bar: this report is a rehearsal of the protocol, not evidence.
robustness.matrix.label: Condition matrix
robustness.cost.label: Cost of adaptation
run.stream.help: Runs this run's weights as {variant}: the state is carried across chunks instead of being reset at every segment. A separate result that is never compared with the offline score.
results.detail.execution.consistent: Chunk consistency: streamed in chunks of {chunk} samples, the outputs match the full-sequence run of the same variant within {tolerance} (max error {error}).
results.detail.execution.inconsistent: Chunk consistency FAILED: streamed in chunks of {chunk} samples, the outputs differ from the full-sequence run by up to {error} (tolerance {tolerance}); the numbers depend on the chunking.
results.detail.execution.note: Look-ahead is the future an output needs (an information bound), not the measured latency of an implementation. The tail is zero-padded at flush.
results.deploy.help: A fixed-point-v1 package: quantised weights, six golden vectors with the state after every sample, a C99 reference verified bit for bit against the software reference, and a report whose numbers say how they were obtained (theoretical, measured execution time, synthesis estimate, measured power). One model, one precision scheme; the rules are pending a maintainer's approval.
results.deploy.unsupported: No fixed-point specification for {model}. fixed-point-v1 covers {supported} (one layer, executed as gru_stream); other models have no deployment export yet.
results.deploy.building: Quantising, replaying golden vectors, compiling the C reference…
results.deploy.verification.bit_exact: Bit-exact: {backend} reference verified on {cases} golden vectors.
results.deploy.verification.mismatch: Mismatch: the {backend} reference differs from the software reference.
results.deploy.verification.not_run: Not verified: the {backend} sources were generated but no C compiler ran them.
results.deploy.mismatch: First difference in case {case} at sample {step}, signal {signal}.
results.deploy.resources: {mac} MAC per sample, {lookups} table lookups per sample; weights {weights} B, state {state} B, tables {tables} B; no sparsity exploited
results.deploy.measured: {rate} samples/s: {what}. A property of this build on this machine, not of a deployment.
results.deploy.notMeasuredPower: not available: nothing was measured; energy is never inferred from MAC or parameter counts
inspection.constellationNote: Dataset-specific demodulation. Output uses input-referenced equalization; the plot is not a standard EVM measurement.
inspection.iqNote: Sampled baseband I/Q, not demodulated symbol constellations. Known reference symbols and a receiver are required for symbol EVM.
inspection.measurementNote: ACPR: negative dBc, lower is better. Hover or focus a value for its measurement conditions.
inspection.noPlots: Charts require finite, paired I/Q samples. Check Dataset Doctor for details.
inspection.window: Capture window {start}–{end} / {total} samples · charts are subsampled; metrics use the full analysis window.
datasets.builtin.title: Built-in datasets
datasets.builtin.help: Choose any dataset shipped with this OpenDPD installation. Adding one copies it into the current workspace.
datasets.create.title: Create Your Own Dataset
datasets.create.help: One row is one paired PA input/output sample, in capture time order. Choose either of these layouts.
datasets.create.formatHelp: Comma-separated UTF-8; optional unique headers. Complex cells accept i or j and scientific notation. The examples show the format only; provide a complete capture.
datasets.create.csvOnly: Choose a .csv file. Export spreadsheets as CSV UTF-8 (comma delimited).
datasets.create.valid: All {count} sample rows passed. Confirm the input/output column roles before continuing.
datasets.create.splitHelp: Keep samples in time order. Percentages apply after two boundary guards are excluded; the shared split protocol calculates the exact counts.
datasets.create.numbers: Enter three positive percentages and a non-negative whole number for the guard.
datasets.create.guardHelp: Default: {count} samples at each boundary. Guards isolate overlapping training frames; keep them at least as long as your frame length.
datasets.create.idHelp: 1–64 characters: letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores; start with a letter or digit.
datasets.create.signalHelp: Enter known physical values only. Without a sample rate, the spectrum uses normalized frequency. Imported CSVs show raw I/Q unless a receiver/reference waveform is bound.
datasets.create.signalInvalid: Use positive finite numbers; carrier count and FFT length must be whole numbers.
datasets.create.ready: Validated {count} paired samples. Review the split before creating the dataset.
datasets.create.guardReview: {count} guard samples at each boundary ({total} excluded from training/validation/test). Raw samples remain intact.
datasets.create.afterCreate: The original CSV is preserved with its hash. Next, inspect the signal, add any missing metadata, then configure an experiment.
datasets.create.fixSamples: Use finite, non-empty decimal or scientific numbers within the float32 range. Complex cells accept a+bj or a+bi. Correct the paired source sample; do not leave blanks, NaN or infinity.
datasets.create.fixFormat: Export a UTF-8 comma-delimited CSV with two complex or four real columns. Check quotes, separators and file availability.
datasets.create.fixRow: Make every row contain exactly the selected number of fields. Restore missing samples, remove extra separators and blank lines, and keep input/output pairs aligned.
datasets.create.fixMapping: Use unique non-empty column names and assign each input/output role to a different column. Set the first row correctly as header or data.
datasets.create.fixSplit: Enter three positive percentages summing to 100%. Supply enough data for non-empty splits and both guards; choose guards that isolate your training frames.
datasets.create.fixEmpty: Add a complete paired input/output capture below the optional header. The file needs more than headers or a format illustration.

tasks.train_pa.help: Learn the PA response from paired input and output samples.
tasks.evaluate_pa.help: Compare a trained PA model with the dataset’s output on the test split.
tasks.train_dpd.help: Train a predistorter using a previously trained PA model.
tasks.run_dpd.help: Apply a trained DPD and test it through a PA model. This is a model-based test.
tasks.model.help: Choose the model to train. Its parameters are available in the next step.
tasks.startingSettings.help: Choose a starting point, then adjust the hyperparameters in the next step.
tasks.threads.help: Leave empty to use the runtime default.
testing.model.help: Choose a successfully completed training run.
testing.model.none: Train a model first, then return here to test it.
testing.surrogate.help: Use the PA model used during DPD training, or another trained PA model on this dataset.
testing.trainingSurrogate: PA model used during DPD training
testing.frozen: The trained weights, architecture and frame settings are reused. Choose how to execute and score the test below.
testing.execution.help: Streaming is offered only when a compatible implementation exists for these weights.
testing.chunk.help: Leave empty to use the shared streaming default.
json.title: Advanced configuration · JSON
json.help: Edit or import a configuration. Applying it replaces this form’s configuration and runs the same server validation before you can submit.
guide.title: Create your first dataset
guide.intro: We’ll walk through the actual setup together. Use your CSV, or try a built-in dataset if you don’t have one yet.
guide.file: Choose the file and check the input/output columns.
guide.split: Set the train, validation and test proportions.
guide.review: Review the sample counts, then create the dataset.
guide.ready.title: Your dataset is ready to inspect
guide.ready.body: Inspect the signals and metadata on this page. The checks explain anything missing. Once the dataset is ready, select Train PA & DPD Models to continue.
guide.builtin.help: Choose any dataset to try. MyCustomPA is synthetic tutorial data. Add opens it for inspection; it does not start training.
guide.csv.file: Step 1 · Upload a CSV with paired input/output samples. We check every row and help you fix any format problems before continuing.
guide.csv.split: Step 2 · Keep the suggested split or adjust it. Give the dataset a name. Signal metadata can be added here or later.
guide.csv.review: Step 3 · Check the final sample counts. Create dataset saves it and opens the signal inspection page.
chart.controls.summary: Two fingers: pan · Pinch or Ctrl/Cmd + wheel: zoom · Double-click: fit
chart.controls.pan: Pan: move two fingers on a trackpad, scroll the wheel, or drag the plot. Shift + wheel pans horizontally.
chart.controls.zoom: Zoom: pinch on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl/Cmd while scrolling. Zoom follows the pointer.
chart.controls.mouse: Mouse: select the zoom tool for box zoom and direct wheel zoom. The mode bar also has zoom and fit buttons.
chart.controls.keyboard: Keyboard: focus the plot, then use arrows to pan, + / − to zoom, Home or 0 to fit, P to pan, and Z to select zoom.
chart.controls.page: Page scrolling: scroll outside the plotting area, or hold Alt while scrolling over a plot.
terminal.independent: These tabs switch logs only; your experiment page stays where it is.
terminal.empty: No run in this step yet. Its terminal will appear when you start an experiment.
live.title: Live experiment
live.geometry: {samples} complex I/Q samples per batch @ {rate} · each sample contains I and Q
live.stride: Frame stride {stride} samples; overlapping samples count again
live.waitingGeometry: Waiting for the worker to build the data loaders…
live.cadence: Signal preview: at least {batches} batches and {seconds} s between updates; adapts to model cost. First batch is shown immediately.
live.surrogate: DPD output is evaluated through the trained PA model (also called a surrogate). These plots show the signal chain predicted by that model.
live.finalHelp: Stored test-split plots from the evaluated checkpoint and the shared metric service.
live.probeHelp: Signal excerpt from {source} · {samples} I/Q samples. Metrics above use the full evaluation split.
live.waitingSignals: The first computed signal preview will appear here.
live.unavailable: The live snapshot could not be loaded. Progress and terminal logs remain available.
about.title: About
about.description: An open framework for power amplifier modelling and digital predistortion. Developed by the Lab of Efficient Machine Intelligence, Delft University of Technology.
about.refreshNote: Checks GitHub every five minutes while this page is open. Contribution totals may be cached by GitHub. Last successful check
about.offline: GitHub is currently unavailable. Any displayed activity is the last successful snapshot; repository links still work.
live.padding: Includes {count} zero-padding samples in the final evaluation sequence.
home.intro: An open-source workspace for power amplifier modeling and digital predistortion, developed by EMI Lab at TU Delft.
home.start.hint: Start with a built-in example or your own CSV.
home.workflow.label: Your experiment, step by step
home.workflow.data.help: Explore a built-in dataset or your own capture.
home.workflow.pa.help: Train a model and validate its response.
home.workflow.dpd.help: Learn a predistorter and evaluate linearization.
chart.recovery.note: If no point or curve is visible, or more than {threshold}% of the view falls outside the data bounds, fit after {delay} s without input. Applies to this chart; turn off to explore empty areas.
reset.warning: This will discard all setup progress on this page. This cannot be undone.
reset.busy: A save or submission is in progress. You can continue when it finishes, or cancel this dialog.
reset.done: Reset complete. You can start over.
reset.page.dataset: You will return to Datasets to choose or create a dataset again.
reset.page.experiment: You will return to the first setup step for this experiment type.
reset.page.results: You will return to Results with the current result and comparison selections cleared.
home.start.builtinHint: Start with a built-in example. Custom datasets are coming soon.
guide.builtin.intro: Start with a built-in dataset, inspect its signals, then configure your first experiment. Custom dataset uploads are coming soon.
guide.builtin.inspect: Inspect the time-domain, spectrum and signal quality.
guide.builtin.configure: Configure PA modeling and DPD experiments.
terminal.title: Terminal
chart.history.title: {metric} per epoch
about.original: Commit titles are shown in their original language.
logs.original: Original process output · commands and library messages retain their source language.
language.loadFailed: Could not load the selected language. Try again.
web.description: Explore built-in datasets and run analysis, neural network training and inference. Computation runs on our isolated server.
web.temporary: During this trial, 2 hours without user activity from an IP causes all temporary workspaces associated with that IP to be deleted. Background refreshes and running jobs do not extend this period. Workspaces are also cleared every 12 hours. The top bar shows the next cleanup deadline; download your data and models before then. CSV datasets are validated; code uploads are unavailable.
web.retention: Temporary workspace · download your results before {date}. Files are deleted automatically.
web.connection.title: Cannot connect to the compute server
web.connection.hint: Check your network connection and retry. If the domain was recently moved, your network may still have old DNS records; try another network or a trusted DNS resolver.
terminal.readOnly: Read-only output. Use Stop experiment to terminate this run.
run.gpuQueue: The shared GPU runs one experiment at a time. Your experiment is queued; you can leave this page and return to it.
chart.controls.touch: Two fingers: zoom and pan. One finger: scroll the page.
datasets.upload.limit: CSV only: UTF-8, at most 25 MiB and 1,000,000 paired samples.
datasets.upload.checking: Validating file type and every CSV row before preview…
model.download.help: Weights selected by the best validation score so far. Save them before the workspace expires.
model.download.waiting: Available after the first model checkpoint is saved.
model.download.error: Could not check model availability. Retry shortly.
form.preview.epochHelp: Update plots after each epoch using validation results.
form.preview.warning: Frequent batch previews may severely slow down training. Each preview performs extra inference and plot calculations.
live.cadence.batch: Plots update every {batches} batches and at epoch end.
bugs.help: Describe the problem here, then continue on GitHub to review and submit your new issue. You can add screenshots there.
bugs.placeholder: What happened? What did you expect? How can we reproduce it?
bugs.tooLong: This description is too long to transfer. Shorten it, then add the remaining details on GitHub.
review.declaration: These are declared physical conditions. Record the source and reference plane; each revision is retained.
review.deltaHelp: Differences are candidate minus reference. Incompatible results show absolute values only.
review.cursorHelp: Nearest stored bin; no interpolation or metric recalculation.
review.crossHelp: Cross-condition review: inspect trends and condition differences; no best ranking.
session.heading: Measurement sessions
session.independenceHelp: Enter the same acquisition ID for files from one physical capture. Independent captures and training seeds are counted separately; a single capture has no repeatability estimate.
session.title: Session title
session.empty: No session references this capture yet.
measurement.processing.help: Saved with the result. Fractional v2 uses offline interpolation; single-shot playback trims 64 samples at each edge.
measurement.ablation.help: Same retained interval at every stage. Amplitude-only and complex-gain reference fits expose phase error; captures are not normalised. Diagnostic NMSE is separate from profile metrics.
sweep.title: Sweep Board
sweep.intro: Pre-register methods, conditions and budgets. Each cell uses the existing run queue and retains every attempt.
sweep.name: Matrix title
sweep.conditions.help: Each condition needs an independent capture dataset. Declare the varied dimension, acquisition batch and source role before training.
sweep.budget.summary: {train} training/fitting runs + {evaluate} evaluations · declared sample × epochs: {samples} · wall-clock limit: {seconds} s
sweep.seedSummary.help: Mean and sample standard deviation of stored metrics across seeds. These are not independent hardware captures. The matrix retains every missing or failed cell.
datasetResearch.syntheticNotice: SYNTHETIC — software demonstration only. These data are not physical measurements and cannot establish RF power, hardware repeatability, efficiency or standard EVM.
datasetResearch.syntheticRecipe: Three normalized drive settings (0.18, 0.26, 0.34), 64QAM OFDM-like input, a causal three-tap polynomial PA and independent noise. The generator version and all seeds are saved.
datasetResearch.useConditions: Use these conditions in Sweep Board
datasetResearch.privateNotice: Data stays in this workspace unless you explicitly submit a public contribution. You can choose public review after uploading.
datasetResearch.localSharing: Public PR submission uses the signed-in GitHub account on local Studio. This temporary web workspace keeps uploads private.
datasetResearch.humanReview: Dataset contributions require human review before merge into the central catalog. For questions, email
datasetResearch.publicNotice: Submitting makes the previewed IQ data, chosen metadata, attribution and license public on GitHub, including while review is pending. The program creates a branch, pushes only the dataset package and opens a PR. It does not merge the PR.
datasetResearch.consent: I have permission to publish this exact data package publicly under the selected license and confirm the attribution.
datasetResearch.choosePublic: After creation, prepare a public contribution for human review
sweep.copiedInitialization: The copied run has initial weights. A matrix must declare its own initialization policy.
sweep.qat.help: Same-condition DPD matrices support qgru/qgru_amp1. This is software fake quantization with FP32 features; accumulator width and hardware cost are not implied. Float pretraining is an additional training budget.
hardware.title: Hardware costs and RF trade-offs
hardware.intro: Compare stored RF results with costs whose source, precision and implementation boundary are stated. A smaller parameter count does not establish lower power.
hardware.chooseRuns: Select runs to inspect their implementation costs.
hardware.missingAxis: No non-stale, sourced cost and released RF metric are available for this axis.
hardware.scatterHelp: Each point corresponds to a numbered evidence card below; hover to see its name. Points are not a ranking; review protocol differences and implementation boundaries.
hardware.reportHelp: Attach the original cost report, then transcribe its values and calculation boundary. These values remain user reported; linking a result does not certify the hardware or its RF performance.
hardware.precisionHelp: One module: format per line, for example weights: INT8. Include features, activations, accumulators and nonlinear functions where applicable.
hardware.invalidNumber: Enter finite numeric values; leave unknown quantities empty.
publication.title: Publication figure
publication.intro: Author up to four panels from saved results. Axes, trace styles and visibility are saved with the figure; display changes never re-score metrics.
publication.private: The full reproduction download includes raw data, checkpoints and private run metadata for every selected run. Keep it private unless you have permission to disclose those files.
results.detail.profile.unavailable: The selected metric profile is not available in the GUI. Choose a released profile; EVM pending independent validation remains unavailable.
hardware.syntheticPlotNotice: This view contains SYNTHETIC / MOCK entries. Inspect each evidence card; these points demonstrate the workflow and do not provide physical validation.
modelWorkflow.paHelp: Train a PA model, then test its predictions in one workspace.
modelWorkflow.dpdHelp: Train a predistorter, then test it with a PA surrogate.
modelWorkflow.sampleHelp: Complex samples after split guards; one sample contains I and Q. Scoring may exclude model warm-up or alignment edges.
modelWorkflow.countError: Could not read the test sample count for this version. Retry by selecting the dataset again.
generator.title: Signal Generator
generator.intro: Create PA input x, inspect its RF characteristics, then choose a Virtual PA to simulate output y.
generator.guideIntro: Start by generating PA input x, or choose an existing dataset / CSV with paired PA input and output.
generator.guideChoose: Choose a signal with ready-to-use settings.
generator.guideInspect: Inspect and download a PA Input Dataset (x).
generator.guideTrain: Choose a Virtual PA and simulate. Studio saves the PA output and paired dataset together, ready for PA / DPD training.
generator.scopeHelp: Synthetic engineering stimuli with NR / WLAN numerology and generic pilots. Continuous uncoded payloads; no complete protocol frames or conformance certification.
generator.lengthLimit: Choose 256–1,000,000 I/Q samples. Duration is converted using the output sample rate, rounded to the nearest sample.
generator.carrierHelp: Saved as RF metadata; exported samples stay at complex baseband.
generator.spacingHelp: Changing spacing sets Fs = spacing × FFT × oversampling.
generator.firstPreview: Choose a waveform, then click Generate to create your PA Input Dataset.
generator.advancedHelp: Customize the waveform geometry and impairments. Modified numerology is labeled custom. Invalid allocations are rejected before generation.
generator.oversamplingHelp: Fs is the output rate. SCS = Fs / (FFT × oversampling). Zero-padding increases time resolution.
generator.channelsHelp: Each allocation is an OFDMA user in one RF band, not a separate RF carrier. Counts include pilots; powers are relative.
generator.pilotIndicesHelp: Comma-separated signed FFT bins, such as -103, -39, 39, 103. Every pilot must belong to an active channel.
generator.configTooLarge: Configuration JSON must be at most 64 KiB.
generator.createHint: At least 8,192 samples. A simulated PA response is added for training.
generator.stale: Parameters changed. Plots still show the last generated signal. Regenerate to update plots, exports and dataset creation.
generator.psdHelp: Welch PSD · Hann window · normalized complex power per Hz.
generator.timeHelp: First {count} contiguous samples; statistics use the complete waveform.
generator.noConstellation: This waveform has no complete modulation symbols to display.
generator.constellationHelp: Data carriers from up to 16 complete OFDM symbols; no equalization.
generator.qamConstellationHelp: Recovered symbols after matched RRC filtering at known timing; edge transients are excluded. Finite-span ISI and impairments remain visible.
generator.ccdfHelp: All samples. Zero probabilities are omitted on the logarithmic plot; empirical resolution is 1/N.
generator.allocationHelp: Crosses mark pilots. Gaps and the DC null carry no symbols. Each row is an independently modulated OFDMA channel.
generator.syntheticPaHelp: Add an illustrative nonlinear memory PA response to this exact stimulus. Both input and output are SYNTHETIC; no hardware measurement is implied.
generator.privateHelp: Private by default. Optional public contribution is available on the dataset page and requires human review. Questions: emi.lab@outlook.com
generator.checkParameters: Check the parameter error on the left, then generate again.
generator.homeHint: Try Signal Generator first — no capture file needed.
generator.dataStepHelp: Generate x and simulate y, or import a paired capture.
paInput.title: PA Input Dataset
paInput.help: This signal contains PA input x only. A complete training dataset needs matching PA input x and PA output y. Measure a real PA, or use the Virtual PA Library to simulate y.
paLibrary.title: PA Library
paLibrary.intro: Choose a Virtual PA, select a PA input dataset, and tune its parameters. One simulation saves the output and paired dataset for model training. Each signal keeps its own sampling rate and starts from zero memory state.
paLibrary.equationHelp: Select a variable, slider or number to highlight the same coefficient. x and y are normalized complex baseband amplitudes; r = |x|. Time constants use µs; Fs is the input sample rate.
paLibrary.range: Enter a value between {min} and {max}. Integer controls require a whole number.
paLibrary.feed: Feed your PA input into this Virtual PA
paLibrary.inputSummary: {count} I/Q samples · {duration} ms · the entire input capture will be simulated.
paLibrary.noInput: Generate a PA Input Dataset first, then select it here. A virtual PA does not create its own input.
paLibrary.stale: The input or PA parameters changed. Simulate again to create output for this configuration.
paLibrary.plotHelp: Metrics use every sample; plots show up to {count} points. Capture: {duration} ms. Input / output RMS: {input} / {output}, normalized units. No device power or efficiency calibration is implied.
paLibrary.pairHelp: Pair the exact input x with this frozen simulated output y. The dataset will be labeled synthetic and retain the signal configuration, Virtual PA formula, parameters and content hashes. Only this step adds it to the training dataset list.
paLibrary.splitHelp: Contiguous splits in time order. Ratios apply after removing two guard intervals; the remainder is testing. Slow physical states can persist beyond a guard interval: this is one continuous synthetic capture, not independent measurements.
paLibrary.splitInvalid: Use a valid dataset ID and name, at least 8,192 input samples, and at least 256 samples per split after guards.
paLibrary.importDisabled: Dataset creation is disabled in this workspace. Input, output and metadata downloads remain available.
paFlow.title: Your PA / DPD workflow
paFlow.trainingHelp: The learned PA surrogate supplies the reference for DPD training.
paFlow.existingHelp: This dataset already supplies paired PA input and output. Dataset making is complete: signal generation and Virtual PA simulation are bypassed. Continue directly with PA model training.
paFlow.generatedHelp: Make PA inputs in Signal Generator, choose a Virtual PA and simulate the outputs. Studio saves the dataset automatically. Then train the PA surrogate and DPD. Checkmarks follow your configuration and successful training runs.
paFlow.begin: Begin with a signal or an existing paired dataset.
spectrum.separated: Separate signal positions · matching initial dB scales · zoom and legend controls are independent. Output targets and with/without-DPD comparisons stay at PA Output.
generator.sharedChannels: Use the same settings for all channels
profile.help: The protocol defines spectral bands, reference power and valid samples. Compare results using the same protocol.
ilc.title: ILC linearization
ilc.help: Learn a PA input waveform by repeated feedback through a trained PA surrogate, then fit an ILA memory-polynomial DPD. ILC is waveform control; train a forward PA model first.
ilc.defaults: Starting settings: 30 iterations, learning gain 0.5, target NMSE −45 dB, peak limit 1.5× training-input peak, 6 backtracking steps. These are conservative starting values, not universally optimal.
ilc.idealHelp: Feedback-optimized on this test waveform through the selected surrogate. This is an achievable reference for this configuration, not a transferable model or measured hardware result.
paInput.removed: PA Input Dataset removed from this workspace.
ilc.summary: Training: {trainReason} · {trainCount} I/Q samples · Testing: {testReason} · {testCount} I/Q samples
ilc.plant: PA: {pa} · Peak limit: {peak} · {calls} test plant calls
server.title: Server load
server.description: Live usage and shared compute availability.
server.staleBody: No recent sample. Utilization is unavailable until telemetry resumes.
server.gpuUnavailable: GPU utilization is not reported by this device or driver. This does not mean zero usage.
server.usersHelp: Estimated from sessions active in the last 5 minutes; one person may have multiple sessions.
server.localUsers: Local mode has no public user count.
server.apiHelp: CPU and memory inside the web service virtual machine.
server.localHelp: Total machine utilization, including other applications.
server.computeHelp: Total host CPU, memory and GPU 0 utilization, including other workloads.
server.privacy: Aggregate data only. Updates every 5 seconds while this page is visible; no user identities or dataset details are shared.
web.expiryHelp: Access ends at this time and automatic file deletion begins. Download your data and models beforehand.
web.queue.title: You are in the waiting room
web.queue.capacity: All workspace slots are occupied. You will enter automatically when a slot becomes available.
web.queue.storage: Temporary storage is currently full. Your place is reserved while space is released.
web.queue.cleanup: Scheduled cleanup is in progress. Admission resumes automatically afterward.
web.queue.help: Keep this tab open. Your position refreshes automatically; refreshing the page keeps your ticket. Disconnected tickets expire after 3 minutes. Compute jobs have a separate queue.
web.end.title: End workspace
web.end.body: Download everything you want to keep first. This ends your session, stops its jobs and deletes its data and results, freeing a workspace for someone else.
web.queue.retrying: Connection or admission is temporarily unavailable. Your request will retry automatically.
web.inactivityHelp: This is the earlier of the shared IP inactivity deadline and scheduled cleanup. User activity can extend the inactivity deadline; automatic refreshes cannot. Download your data and models beforehand.
analyzer.title: Signal Analyzer
analyzer.intro: Choose a dataset, then a signal within it. Confirm its sample rate and bandwidth before analyzing.
analyzer.sourceMissing: This signal is unavailable in the current workspace. Select another source or upload it again.
analyzer.csvHelp: CSV: one real or complex column, or separate I/Q columns. Optional header; select columns for wider files. Up to 25 MiB.
analyzer.rateRequired: CSV contains no sample-rate metadata. Confirm the correct sample rate before measuring.
analyzer.adjacentHelp: Blank uses one measurement bandwidth. Adjacent bands must fit inside Nyquist.
analyzer.referenceHelp: Reference errors require the same sample rate and aligned samples. No timing search or resampling is performed; CSV column choices apply to both signals.
analyzer.stale: Settings changed. Analyze again to update these results.
analyzer.first: Select a signal or upload CSV
analyzer.timeHelp: Time plots show the first 2,048 contiguous samples of the selected range. Low-envelope phase differences are excluded from the frequency display.
analyzer.eyeHelp: Set samples per symbol and timing offset manually. This overlays raw samples without a receiver; an OFDM waveform is not expected to form a single-carrier eye.
analyzer.formulaHelp: x is the analyzed signal; r is the aligned reference. g = 1 unless gain fitting is enabled. w is the selected FFT window. Errors are sample-domain measurements, not protocol EVM.
analyzer.spectrogramHelp: Hover or touch a cell for frequency, time and power density. Every cell averages linear spectral power.
generator.payloadHelp: 1–4,096 binary digits; repeats MSB first. Generic pilots use their own seeded sequence.
generator.burstHelp: RMS is set before gating. Statistics include idle intervals. Payload generation remains continuous; this does not create protocol packets.
generator.phaseNoiseHelp: Gaussian phase jitter per sample; not an oscillator noise mask.
generator.evmTrendHelp: Known-grid diagnostics from at most 16 complete OFDM symbols, without receiver equalization. These are not standard conformance EVM results.
generator.matrixHelp: Pick multiple cells. Columns: baseband bandwidth. Rows: modulation. Each group has a different number of OFDMA channels.
generator.selectedPresets: Selected presets · click to edit or preview
generator.filterHelp: Sharp band edges with a 4% cosine transition. Applies to this preset; turn off for an unfiltered waveform. Filtering can change EVM and burst edges.
generator.selectionLimit: Select up to 16 presets and 4,000,000 total I/Q samples. Hosted workspace storage limits also apply.
generator.batchNext: These are PA inputs only. Choose a Virtual PA next; one simulation creates a complete dataset with one input/output CSV per preset.
paLibrary.batch: All {count} selected presets will use this PA. Each keeps its own sample rate and starts with zero memory state.
paLibrary.autoDataset: Simulating also saves the complete dataset and opens its details. Default split: 60% training, 20% validation, 20% testing with 256-sample guards.
datasets.captureHelp: Charts, metadata, preprocessing and training use the selected subdataset. Each preset retains its own sample rate and length. The collection ZIP contains all original captures and the PA replay script.
spectrum.paModelHelp: PA model (surrogate) is the trained amplifier model. Without DPD: original input → PA model. With DPD: original input → DPD → same PA model. PA-model curves are predictions; dataset curves are labeled measured or synthetic.
profile.spectral: OpenDPD · carrier ACLR on valid samples
waveform.help: Compare the output with its reference, or inspect one signal. I and Q share the same amplitude scale. Zoom or pan to see more detail.
generator.previewIntro: Review generated PA inputs, download signals, or continue with a Virtual PA.
generator.previewSignal: Visualize a Signal in the Generated Dataset
generator.datasetNameHelp: Auto: family, bw (MHz), q/p (modulation), c (channels), s (kHz spacing), n (signals). Ranges summarize the selected specs.
generator.datasetNameInvalid: Start with syn_pa_in_; use letters, numbers, underscores, dots or hyphens (up to 96 characters).
paLibrary.datasetNameHelp: Start with syn_pa_inout_. Each signal keeps its own sampling rate and bandwidth.
